nodes.label: desktop memory - state and handoff docs get the utmost care

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. State-transfer and handoff documents are the most important artifact an agent ever produces in any conversation - the user, 2026-06-14, emphatic: 'the most important part you will ever do in any of our chats, ever.' They are the sole bridge between sessions and agents, so a flaw in them propagates: a single imprecise phrase in a state doc literally seeded a fresh agent's wrong conclusion, where the doc's framing of where a tag's per-facet content comes from presupposed per-facet content the tagger emits and walked the new agent into a fork the project had already rejected. The doc does not just summarize - it constrains what the next agent will conclude. Treat every state or handoff as the highest-stakes deliverable in the chat and do not rush it; audit every framing for hidden presupposition, because an open question phrased one way silently rules an answer in or out, so state open problems neutrally and completely, list the real options including the one consistent with the settled constraints, and explicitly name the rejected framings as traps; separate canon from speculation ruthlessly and never let an assistant guess read as user-confirmed; keep the doc internally consistent and consistent with the live docs and memory; and re-read the finished doc adversarially, as the receiving agent would, asking what wrong conclusion this phrasing could nudge. CANON_AUDIT.md lists this among the grounded, verbatim-quoted and correct desktop entries
